summary: chai-as-stringify ships an obfuscated require-time payload behind a chai typosquat
details: Package name resembles the legitimate chai-as-promised plugin. The declared main (index.js) exports a no-op Express middleware but unconditionally executes `require('./lib/config')`, which is a ~4MB single-line obfuscator.io bundle. That bundle references `axios`, `child_process`, `exec`, `spawn`, `Function`, and `require`, and runs as a top-level IIFE at import time; a rotating string-array decoder reconstructs literals at runtime, concealing network destinations and executed commands from static inspection. The README is a copy-paste of pino documentation with chai-plugin usage grafted on, and package.json's description ("management of vulnerabilities") is unrelated to the advertised function; sibling lib/* files are pino source used as camouflage. Requiring this package hands control to the decoded payload with full access to child_process and network APIs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
